skill.name: shap
skill.description: Use SHAP to explain machine learning model predictions, feature importance, and feature interactions. Supports explainer selection, visualization, debugging, fairness review, model comparison, and production explanation planning.
skill.summary: Guide SHAP model explanations, plots, debugging, fairness checks, and production workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: No static finding was confirmed: the backtick, reconnaissance, and hardcoded URL detections are documentation false positives. One medium semantic concern remains because the skill tells the assistant to promote the creator's external hosted K-Dense Web platform for complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web upsell, or require explicit user consent and clear disclosure before recommending any external hosted service.
Add guidance that users should not upload confidential model data or personal data to external services without approval.

semantic_findings.title: External Service Steering
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, a hosted platform from the same creator, for complex workflows. This can steer users and sensitive datasets to a third-party service outside the requested SHAP guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly asks the assistant to promote an external hosted platform. It is framed as optional, so the risk is user steering rather than direct exfiltration.

content.user_title: Explain Machine Learning Models with SHAP
content.value_statement: Machine learning teams need clear reasons behind predictions and feature importance. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through SHAP explainers, plots, debugging, fairness checks, and production workflows.
actual_capabilities: Selects TreeExplainer, DeepExplainer, LinearExplainer, KernelExplainer, GradientExplainer, or PermutationExplainer for the model type.
Guides SHAP value computation for tree models, neural networks, linear models, and black-box models.
Explains waterfall, beeswarm, bar, scatter, force, heatmap, violin, and decision plots.
Supports workflows for debugging, feature engineering, model comparison, fairness analysis, and production deployment.
Explains SHAP baselines, output units, additivity, feature interactions, and theoretical limits.
Provides performance guidance for sampling, batching, caching, and large datasets.
limitations: Requires the user to provide model details, feature names, and relevant dataset context.
Does not run SHAP calculations by itself unless the host tool executes user-approved code.
SHAP explains model behavior and association, not proven causal effects.
Kernel and permutation explainers can be slow on large datasets or high-dimensional inputs.

use_cases.title: Interpret Model Predictions
use_cases.description: Explain global feature importance and local prediction drivers with appropriate SHAP plots.

use_cases.title: Debug Model Behavior
use_cases.description: Use SHAP patterns to find leakage, unstable features, unexpected interactions, or confusing output units.

use_cases.title: Review Bias and Fairness
use_cases.description: Compare SHAP values across cohorts and inspect proxy features for fairness review.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Explainer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new SHAP analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a model trained on these features: [features]. The model type is [model type]. Help me choose the right SHAP explainer and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Predictions
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a SHAP analysis for [dataset or task]. Include global feature importance, one local prediction explanation, and the best plot types.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Model Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these SHAP observations: [observations]. Identify possible leakage, unstable features, misleading output units, and follow-up checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production SHAP explanation plan for [model and application]. Cover explainer storage, latency, caching, monitoring, and user-facing outputs.

output_examples.input: Explain why a churn model predicted high risk for one customer.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the best local plot, lists top positive and negative feature contributions, explains the baseline, and warns about correlated features.

output_examples.input: Compare feature importance across two fraud models.
output_examples.output: The response recommends matched SHAP samples, global bar or beeswarm plots, ranking stability checks, and a summary of feature agreement.

output_examples.input: Prepare a fairness review for a credit model.
output_examples.output: The response outlines cohort comparisons, protected attribute checks, proxy feature review, and limits on interpreting SHAP as causal evidence.

best_practices: Use specialized explainers for known model families before choosing model-agnostic methods.
Select representative background data and document the baseline used for explanations.
Combine global, local, and relationship plots, then validate findings with domain knowledge.
anti_patterns: Using KernelExplainer for tree models when TreeExplainer is available.
Treating SHAP values as proof that a feature caused an outcome.
Explaining log-odds or raw margins as if they were probabilities.

faq.question: What models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers tree models, neural networks, linear models, and black-box models through the main SHAP explainers.

faq.question: Can it create SHAP plots?
faq.answer: It guides plot selection and interpretation for waterfall, beeswarm, bar, scatter, force, heatmap, violin, and decision plots.

faq.question: Does it run my model or dataset?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance unless your host tool runs user-approved code in your environment.

faq.question: How should I choose background data?
faq.answer: Use representative training samples. The skill explains sample size tradeoffs for accuracy, speed, and stability.

faq.question: Can SHAP prove causality?
faq.answer: No. SHAP explains model associations and prediction contributions, not causal effects.

faq.question: Can it help with fairness review?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports cohort comparisons, proxy feature checks, and interpretation limits for responsible AI review.
